To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
primary school teachers reported applying antecedents based CMSs most frequently and secondary school teachers reported applying self regulation CMSs most frequently for students with symptoms ADHD.
Teachers reported applying antecdent based CMSs the most and self regulation CMS the least, which was also in accordance with the effectiveness of these types.
Primary and secondary school teachers reported applying antecedents based CMSs most frequently, whereas self regulation CMSs were reported to be used least frequently.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what the role of teachers is in relation to ADHD symptoms.
the use of evidence based CMS for students with ADHD in Dutch schools.
the use and effectiveness of classroom management strategies ( CMSs ) for students with symptoms Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder ( ADHD ) in Dutch primary and secondary education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
teachers' reported frequency and perceived effectiveness of CMS for students with ADHD does not match the evidence based findings.
teachers do not use CMSs in a way that is in line with the evidence base, and that they are not very positive about the effectiveness of CMSs in general.
teachers use the evidence based classroom management strategies less frequently and less effectively than the research literature indicates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effectiveness of CMSs in the classroom is not only a function of the strategy itself but also of the teachers who use them.
we found that teachers' use and effectiveness of classroom management strategies for students with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder do not conform to the evidence-based effectiveness.
we have shown that teachers are not using the strategies they should be and that they are not seeing them as effective.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of evidence based CMS for students with ADHD should be emphasized during teacher training and that teachers should be informed that students with ADHD may need additional support.
the effectiveness of evidence based strategies should be considered in the training of teachers and that training should focus on the adaptation of strategies to individual student characteristics.
teachers should be provided with training on the most effective CMSs for students, including students with ADHD.
